newsitem.title: CANADA: PanCanadian pulls plug on Libya oil play.
newsitem.headline: PanCanadian pulls plug on Libya oil play.

text.p: PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd has quietly given up a stake in an exploration project in Libya, PanCanadian chief executive David Tuer said on Thursday.
Tuer said Calgary-based PanCanadian allowed partner Fina France SA to assume its 15 percent stake in a Sirte Basin exploration play about one month ago for no financial consideration.
The partners had completed 10 wells in a 12-well program and only one had encountered hydrocarbons, albeit in uncommercial quantities, PanCanadian spokesman Rick Jeffrey said.

Tuer said PanCanadian, which is still involved in one Libyan exploration project, was not subject to U.S. sanctions against companies that did business with the North African country because agreements were in place before the U.S. moves were made.
Investments were also well below the US$40 million sanction threshold, he said.
